faq.a: 4500×5400 px at 300 DPI (15×18 inches), as a transparent PNG. That is a common full-size front print area on t-shirts and a size many print-on-demand services recommend working at. Check your platform's current rules, because some accept other sizes.
Black areas vanish on a black shirt and white areas vanish on a white one, so the palette is adjusted to the fabric.

faq.q: Can I sell shirts with these designs?
faq.a: Yes, as long as your description doesn't copy trademarks, logos or existing artwork. Platforms remove infringing listings, so describe an original idea.
Yes. PiCraft removes the background automatically and exports a PNG with transparency, so only the artwork is printed. Preview it over a dark and a light color to confirm.

faq.q: Does it work with Merch on Demand, Printful and Redbubble?
faq.a: Yes, all of them accept transparent PNG files. Their rules change over time, so check each platform's current requirements for size, color space and file weight before you upload.

faq.q: Can I use the design on other products?
faq.a: Yes, for example on tote bags, hoodies or mugs. Scale the file to the print area of the product. The shape is tuned for a shirt front, so wide products may need the design cropped or resized.

faq.q: How sharp will the design print?
faq.a: The 4500×5400 px file is upscaled from the generated design. Bold shapes and flat colors print sharply, while fine texture and tiny text can look soft. Order a sample shirt to check.

faq.q: What about shirts that are neither black nor white?
faq.a: The palette is tuned for dark or light fabric. For a mid-tone shirt such as red or green, choose the option closer to it and check the result on a mockup.

faq.q: Why did the slogan come out wrong?
faq.a: Text inside AI images can contain mistakes. Keep slogans short, read every letter and generate again if something is off.
